 16 June 2025 
 Welsh translation added. 
 
 
 9 June 2025 
 The section 'When you must account for import VAT on your VAT Return' has been removed, as this procedure is no longer mandatory. Information about using another person or business to import goods for you has been updated, as they must now have written permission to use postponed VAT accounting. 
 
 
 1 October 2022 
 Information about Customs Handling of Import and Export Freight (CHIEF) has been removed. You can no longer use CHIEF for import declarations unless you have permission from HMRC. 
 
 
 15 December 2021 
 Existing arrangements for customs checks on goods from Ireland will continue after 1 January 2022. Changes made to "When you must account for import VAT on your VAT return" and "How to complete your customs declaration account for import VAT on your VAT Return". 
 
 
 13 August 2021 
 Clarification that postponed VAT accounting will be available permanently. A checklist has been added to help navigation, and the details you may need to complete your customs declaration using CHIEF have been updated. 
 
 
 8 April 2021 
 The 'If you import goods for business and non-business purposes' section has been updated to say you can account for import VAT on your VAT return if you import goods that will be used solely for a non-business purpose, and you are a body that is eligible to reclaim import VAT through a VAT refund scheme . The 'How to complete your customs declaration to account for import VAT on your VAT Return' section has also been updated with information about selecting how to account for import VAT on your customs declaration. 
 
 
 16 March 2021 
 The end date when you must account for import VAT on your VAT Return if you delay your customs declaration or use a simplified customs declaration has been changed from 30 June 2021 to 31 December 2021. 
 
 
 11 February 2021 
 There have been multiple changes to this guidance to help readers understand what they need to do and how to do it. 
 
 
 22 December 2020 
 Information has been added about accounting for VAT if you do not know the full customs value of goods and using someone to import goods on your behalf. 
 
 
 4 December 2020 
 Information on Non-established taxable persons and guidance on how to complete your declaration if you are accounting for import VAT on your VAT return has been added. 
 
 
 24 August 2020 
 Added Welsh translation. 
 
 
 27 July 2020 
 First published.
blocks.section: Updates to this page

blocks.text: Accounting for import VAT on your VAT Return means you declare and recover import VAT on the same VAT Return, rather than paying it upfront when the goods are imported and recovering it later. It is also called postponed VAT accounting.
blocks.section: Updates to this page

blocks.text: The normal rules about what VAT you can reclaim as input tax apply.
blocks.section: Updates to this page

blocks.text: Before using postponed VAT accounting
blocks.section: Before using postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: Your business must be registered for VAT in the UK to use postponed VAT accounting.
blocks.section: Before using postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: Who can use postponed VAT accounting
blocks.section: Who can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: You can account for import VAT on your VAT Return for goods you import into:
blocks.section: Who can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: Great Britain (England, Scotland and Wales) from anywhere outside the UK
blocks.section: Who can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: Northern Ireland from outside the UK and EU
blocks.section: Who can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: You do not need any approval to account for import VAT on your VAT Return.
blocks.section: Who can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: Non-established taxable persons
blocks.section: Non-established taxable persons

blocks.text: If you are a person who does not have a UK establishment, you’ll need to get someone to deal with customs for you . They’ll also need to complete your import declaration.
blocks.section: Non-established taxable persons

blocks.text: If you want to account for import VAT on your VAT Return, you must tell the person dealing with customs on your behalf to both:
blocks.section: Non-established taxable persons

blocks.text: select this on your import declaration
blocks.section: Non-established taxable persons

blocks.text: enter your details as the consignee
blocks.section: Non-established taxable persons

blocks.text: If someone imports goods on your behalf
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: You can have a person or business import goods on your behalf. For example, this could be:
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: a freight forwarder
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: a customs agent
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: a broker
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: an express operator
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: When someone imports goods on your behalf, you’ll need to tell them, in writing, if you want to use postponed VAT accounting on those imports. They must have this written confirmation before they can proceed with the import declaration.
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: If you already have someone importing goods on your behalf, you should contact them to tell them if you want to use postponed VAT accounting on imports. You should keep a written record of your instructions.
blocks.section: If someone imports goods on your behalf

blocks.text: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf
blocks.section: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf

blocks.text: You can also buy goods from a supplier who arranges for a person or business to import and deliver the goods for you.
blocks.section: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf

blocks.text: You must agree with the supplier how you want to account for import VAT. This is so that they can give the person or business importing the goods written instructions to make the correct entry on the import declaration. They must have these written instructions before they can make the import declaration. Keep a written record of what you agree with the supplier.
blocks.section: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf

blocks.text: You’ll also need to give the supplier your EORI number.
blocks.section: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf

blocks.text: The import will appear on your monthly postponed import VAT statement in the normal way.
blocks.section: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf

blocks.text: Check your import VAT certificate (C79) and postponed VAT account statements using the Customs Declaration Service, to make sure all your imports are covered. Businesses should check their financial dashboard for their statements.
blocks.section: When a supplier arranges for someone to import goods on your behalf

blocks.text: When you can use postponed VAT accounting
blocks.section: When you can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: You can do this if both the following apply:
blocks.section: When you can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: the goods you import are for use in your business and you have the right to dispose of them (usually as the owner)
blocks.section: When you can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: you include your VAT registration number on your import declaration
blocks.section: When you can use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: If you import goods for business and non-business purposes
blocks.section: If you import goods for business and non-business purposes

blocks.text: You can account for import VAT on your VAT Return if you import goods which:
blocks.section: If you import goods for business and non-business purposes

blocks.text: will be used for both business and non-business purposes
blocks.section: If you import goods for business and non-business purposes

blocks.text: you do not know will be used for business purposes at the time that you import them
blocks.section: If you import goods for business and non-business purposes

blocks.text: You can use postponed VAT accounting when you import goods you know will be used solely for non-business purposes, but only if you’re a body that is eligible to reclaim import VAT through a VAT refund scheme . When you complete your import declaration, select that you’re making an immediate payment, or using a duty deferment account.
blocks.section: If you import goods for business and non-business purposes

blocks.text: Goods in special procedures
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: If you declare goods into a customs special procedure , you can select that you’ll be accounting for import VAT on your VAT Return when you submit the declaration that removes them into free circulation. This applies to the following special procedures:
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: customs warehousing
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: inward processing
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: temporary admission
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: end use
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: outward processing
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: duty suspension
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: Find out about trading and moving goods in and out of Northern Ireland if you move goods between Northern Ireland and the EU.
blocks.section: Goods in special procedures

blocks.text: Excise goods
blocks.section: Excise goods

blocks.text: You can account for import VAT on your VAT Return when you release excise goods for use in the UK . This is also known as goods ‘released for home consumption’.
blocks.section: Excise goods

blocks.text: This includes when goods are released from an excise warehouse after being in duty suspension since they were imported.
blocks.section: Excise goods

blocks.text: Imports delivered by Royal Mail Group
blocks.section: Imports delivered by Royal Mail Group

blocks.text: If your business receives goods through the post in consignments of more than £135 using Royal Mail Group (including Parcelforce, where they are not acting as an express operator) you cannot account for import VAT on your VAT Return.
blocks.section: Imports delivered by Royal Mail Group

blocks.text: Royal Mail Group offers postponed VAT accounting for commercial (non-postal) services, if requested by the importer.
blocks.section: Imports delivered by Royal Mail Group

blocks.text: If you do not know the full customs value of goods
blocks.section: If you do not know the full customs value of goods

blocks.text: You can still account for import VAT on your VAT Return, even if you cannot confirm the full customs value of the goods that you import.
blocks.section: If you do not know the full customs value of goods

blocks.text: To do this, you should:
blocks.section: If you do not know the full customs value of goods

blocks.text: Apply for a general guarantee account to cover the amount of VAT that is unknown.
blocks.section: If you do not know the full customs value of goods

blocks.text: Select that you’ll be accounting for import VAT on your VAT Return for the amount that is known.
blocks.section: If you do not know the full customs value of goods

blocks.text: How to use postponed VAT accounting on your import declaration
blocks.section: How to use postponed VAT accounting on your import declaration

blocks.text: When completing your import declaration, you can select to account for import VAT on your VAT Return. You cannot change how you want to account for import VAT on your import declaration once you’ve submitted it.
blocks.section: How to use postponed VAT accounting on your import declaration

blocks.text: You need to enter your VAT registration number at header level in Data Element 3/40 (you should not use method of payment G in Data Element 4/8).
blocks.section: How to use postponed VAT accounting on your import declaration

blocks.text: VAT will be recorded against your EORI number. This will be at declaration level only.
blocks.section: How to use postponed VAT accounting on your import declaration

blocks.text: If you act on behalf of someone else
blocks.section: If you act on behalf of someone else

blocks.text: If you’ve been authorised to act on behalf of your client, you must use their EORI number or VAT registration number on the import declaration.
blocks.section: If you act on behalf of someone else

blocks.text: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less
blocks.section: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less

blocks.text: There are different rules for the treatment of goods in consignments valued at £135 or less.
blocks.section: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less

blocks.text: Find out about the treatment of VAT for imported goods sold:
blocks.section: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less

blocks.text: to customers in the UK using online marketplaces
blocks.section: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less

blocks.text: directly to customers in the UK
blocks.section: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less

blocks.text: These rules do not apply to the import of excise goods. You can choose to account for import VAT on your VAT Return for the import of consignments of excise goods of any value.
blocks.section: If you import goods in consignments valued at £135 or less

blocks.text: If you import commercial goods (merchandise in baggage) into Great Britain or Northern Ireland
blocks.section: If you import commercial goods (merchandise in baggage) into Great Britain or Northern Ireland

blocks.text: If you’re eligible to make a simple online declaration instead and choose to do so, you will not be able to account for import VAT on your VAT Return.
blocks.section: If you import commercial goods (merchandise in baggage) into Great Britain or Northern Ireland

blocks.text: Find out more about:
blocks.section: If you import commercial goods (merchandise in baggage) into Great Britain or Northern Ireland

blocks.text: bringing commercial goods into Great Britain in your baggage
blocks.section: If you import commercial goods (merchandise in baggage) into Great Britain or Northern Ireland

blocks.text: bringing commercial goods into Northern Ireland in your baggage
blocks.section: If you import commercial goods (merchandise in baggage) into Great Britain or Northern Ireland

blocks.text: What you’ll need to do if you choose to use postponed VAT accounting
blocks.section: What you’ll need to do if you choose to use postponed VAT accounting

blocks.text: You can get your postponed import VAT statements online , which you can use to help you when completing your VAT Return to account for import VAT .
blocks.section: What you’ll need to do if you choose to use postponed VAT accounting
